result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A puts the whole page in bakery terms. It uses café sample rows, loaf and pastry items and Pending/Baking/Ready/Delivered stages, and its no-match and delete messages name the search, order and café. Answer B keeps 'Customer 1', 'Product A' and the generic 'No results found.', and its statuses are not bake stages. B does have the better 4 a.m. feature, a to-bake total per product, and it stays closer to the original markup. Still, it misses the main ask of making the page fit the bakery. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer A still says Customer 1, Product A and Pending/Complete, and leaves 'No results found.' generic, so the page still feels like a template.
